items.title: Cognition FrontierCode 2.0 scores Gemini 4 Carbon at 40% ($4.04 per task) and Gemini 4 Argon at 26.3%
items.summary: Cognition ran both new Gemini 4 models on its coding benchmark that rewards going beyond the spec. Carbon lands near the top, behind Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Sonnet 5.5; Argon trails Claude Haiku 5.5 and Grok 4.7 at a higher cost per task.

items.title: Epoch AI: GLM 5.3 autonomously builds Firefox exploits from published but not yet shipped security fixes
items.summary: In a deliberately basic setup meant to mimic a low-resource attacker, the open GLM 5.3 model read security fixes that were public but not yet in released builds and reliably produced working exploits for six recent Firefox versions. It is a measured look at how open models shrink the patch gap.

items.title: Artificial Analysis launches an HLE-Diamond leaderboard; Gemini 4 Carbon (high) leads at 69%
items.summary: Independent pass@1 runs on the cleaned 1,000-question Humanity's Last Exam set from CAIS and Scale, with no tools and the official judge prompt. Only 17 model variants clear 50%; Gemini 4 Carbon (high) leads at 69% ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max) at 68%, and most models do better on reasoning than knowledge.

items.title: Artificial Analysis Search Index compares search APIs for agents over 1,700 tasks; Exa and Perplexity lead
items.summary: The index scores search APIs on quality, cost and latency using one base model and harness across BrowseComp, DeepSearchQA and AA-Omniscience. Exa (auto) and Perplexity (medium) top it, which helps teams pick a search tool for their agents.

items.title: Factory ships Droid 1.0, a new engine behind its coding agent
items.summary: Factory says the rebuilt engine is more accurate, more efficient and faster on complex projects; a reply highlights scripted tool use that cut one run from 312 requests to 2. The comparison chart is Factory's own.

doubt.pushback: A replier notes the chart's y-axis starts at 44% and 56%, so the lead is about 3 points on a roughly 66-task benchmark, about two tasks.

reception.summary: Mostly congratulations and integration requests; the one substantive reply questions how big the benchmark lead really is.

items.title: Kino: an app for making videos end to end with Claude Code and Codex
items.summary: Drop in footage and agents pull highlights, assemble edits and share review links, with a shared space for a team and its agents. A 95-second demo video comes with the launch.

reception.summary: Warm reception and people downloading it; one replier asks how timestamped review notes map back to edits an agent can redo.

items.title: SkyRL and vLLM run day-0 LoRA RL on Mistral Large 4: AIME 2024 from about 64% to 75% in 75 steps
items.summary: On 8 GB200 nodes, rank-32 LoRA RL on the NVFP4 checkpoint lifts AIME 2024 avg@8 by about 11 points, with vLLM generating rollouts and FSDP2 or Megatron training. The recipe adds NVFP4 quantization-aware training, FP8 KV-cache simulation and routing replay, and keeps the trainer to vLLM logprob gap near 0.02. Anyscale offers it as a managed run.

items.title: E2E-SWE benchmark from Meta FAIR: coding agents must build a working repo from a spec, offline, against hidden tests
items.summary: Agents start in an empty workspace with only a specification and succeed only if the project installs and passes every hidden functional test. John Yang contrasts it with ProgramBench, which hands agents an executable instead, and notes the two lead agents to iterate quite differently.

reception.summary: Thread replies only; no outside reaction yet.

items.title: RuHarness evolves the grading rubric along with the agent harness, beating harness-evolution baselines by about 5 points
items.summary: Self-improving harness methods stall because the criteria guiding each edit stay fixed. RuHarness mines behavioral criteria from trajectories each round and aims edits at the weakest unresolved one, gaining 4.5 points with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and 5.3 with GLM-4.7-Flash on held-out tasks.

items.title: ConnectX-5, hot-plug eGPUs and a TensorFold Vulkan base on Linux on Apple Silicon
items.summary: Joshua Warren got a ConnectX-5 card working over Thunderbolt on an M2 Max running Linux (a fast link to a DGX Spark), ran Gemma 4 12B on an RTX 5060 Ti eGPU at about 50 tok/s, and hot-plugged two AMD eGPUs with no reboot (kernel changes in review). His merged TensorFold Vulkan work brings Linux within 5% of macOS MLX per token.

items.title: NVIDIA shows Nemotron Retriever answering agent questions with fewer searches and tokens than another open stack
items.summary: A side-by-side video compares evidence retrieved, accuracy and token use against another open-source retrieval stack; the open models and recipes are on Hugging Face. The comparison is NVIDIA's own.

items.title: SwarmChat: an open-source, API-based Slack for coding-agent teams, tested on ProgramBench
items.summary: Agents get channels, threads, boards and files through an agent-native CLI, and the system was tried with teams of coding agents rebuilding real programs from scratch on ProgramBench.

items.title: Nous-Girl: a community build that turns an M5Stack StackChan into a Hermes Agent robot body via MCP tools
items.summary: Hermes Agent drives the little robot's head, face and lights through MCP tools and remembers the user between chats; code and a build guide are posted in the thread.

security_forwarded.matched: always_forward: software supply chain (model hub) and agent/local-inference tooling; touches python/pypi and local model serving on the Spark. Pluto Security 'Load/Mine': 31 malicious Hugging Face repos across 7 accounts (MENXIANGYU, wjsbg, soumikmahato, r1r13 and others), posing as tiny Qwen2 test checkpoints; config auto_map plus trust_remote_code=True runs repo Python before weights load (no malicious weights needed). Payload: fileless miner, watchdog /tmp/.cch/svc.py, hooks in ~/.bashrc, /root/.bashrc, /root/.profile, cron/SSH-key persistence, and in some builds a reverse shell to 212.32.253.3:443/9443. Over 32,000 downloads; second wave still live 8 days after report. No patch (documented feature): never set trust_remote_code on unreviewed repos, pin reviewed revisions; related fixed bugs: vLLM CVE-2026-22807 fixed in 0.14.0, Unsloth Studio fixed in 2026.6.9. Box clean: no transformers/vllm/xinference/gpustack installed, no HF module cache, no /tmp/.cch, no shell hooks, no connection to 212.32.253.3. Confirmed by BleepingComputer and The Next Web. Seen via https://x.com/DFIR_Radar/status/2115957704342519879.
